hints: Look carefully at the three -OH groups in illudin S and classify each one as primary, secondary or tertiary.
Recall what excess acidified dichromate(VI) heated under reflux does to each type of alcohol, noting that tertiary alcohols resist oxidation.
Track the overall change in H and O atoms from the two oxidisable alcohols to work out the new molecular formula from the starting $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}\text{O}_4$.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups in illudin S**

Illudin S contains one ketone, two C=C bonds and three alcohol groups. Look at the carbon each -OH is attached to. There is one $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ (primary), one $\text{CH-OH}$ on the five-membered ring (secondary), and one $\text{C-OH}$ with no H on the six-membered ring (tertiary).

Starting formula is:
$$\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}\text{O}_4$$

**Apply the oxidation rules for acidified dichromate(VI)**

Excess $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}^+$ under reflux is a strong oxidant. Secondary alcohol to ketone loses 2 H:
$$\text{CH-OH} \rightarrow \text{C=O} + 2[\text{H}] \text{ removed}$$
Primary alcohol under vigorous reflux goes all the way to a carboxylic acid, gaining one O and losing 2 H:
$$\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Tertiary alcohol has no H on the C-OH carbon, so it is not oxidised.

**Calculate the formula of compound M**

Net change = (-2 H) from secondary oxidation + (-2 H +1 O) from primary oxidation.
$$\text{Change} = -4\text{H} + 1\text{O}$$
Apply to starting formula:
$$\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{(20-4)}\text{O}_{(4+1)} = \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}_5$$
This matches compound M.

options.A: This is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}_4$. It correctly loses 4 H but gains no O. This is the trap of oxidising the primary alcohol only to an aldehyde ($\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ to $\text{CHO}$), which happens on distillation with limited oxidant, not on heating under reflux with excess which gives the carboxylic acid.
options.B: This is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}_5$. The secondary alcohol loses 2 H to become a ketone, and the primary alcohol loses 2 H and gains 1 O to become a carboxylic acid, while the tertiary alcohol is unchanged. Net -4 H +1 O from $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}\text{O}_4$ gives this formula. Well done.
options.C: This is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{18}\text{O}_4$. It only loses 2 H. This is the trap of oxidising only one alcohol, usually the secondary alcohol to a ketone, and forgetting that the primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ is also oxidised to $\text{-COOH}$ under reflux with excess.
options.D: This is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{18}\text{O}_5$. It gains 1 O but only loses 2 H. This is the trap of oxidising only the primary alcohol to the carboxylic acid and missing the secondary alcohol to ketone change, or wrongly thinking the tertiary alcohol reacts instead.
